text: Add 2-3 real Music Lab levels from the 'Songwriter's Toolbox' family (Coding with Music lesson 1) -- search the catalog and attach them in their original order, at the start of this lesson. Use canonical/base level keys.

Added 3 real Music Lab levels at the start of Studio Day 1, all confirmed Music type: `coding-with-music-play-sound` → `play-two` → `play-together`, matching the natural difficulty progression (one sound → two sounds → playing them together) from the "Songwriter's Toolbox" lesson. These are the canonical base keys — no year/grade duplicates existed for this family, and I used the non-standalone `play-together` (not the `-standalone` variant) since it's meant to run in sequence here, not as a decoupled freeplay activity.

Create a small interactive widget at the end of this lesson: a 2-item trace-prediction check where students predict what a shown 4-block program does before running it (blocks like play a note, wait, play a note, wait -- or similar simple sequence blocks). Kind, encouraging feedback either way. Keyboard accessible, no network.

Build succeeded, no errors. Added "Predict the Trace" at the end of Studio Day 1 — the wrap widget the lesson overview already referenced. Two items: students read a shown 4-block program (Play Note / Wait chips, numbered in order) and pick from 3 choices what it will actually do before it runs — same note twice with a pause between, then two different notes back-to-back followed by a pause. Feedback is kind either way (a correct "Yes!" or a gentle "Nice try!" that walks through the real trace, never harsh). Built as a TSX package using real `GenericButton` and `Alert` components, with the block-chip display styled from design tokens since no component covers that; correctness logic is pulled into a small tested `logic.ts`. Keyboard-operable throughout, emits `predicted`/`completed` events, no network.
